answer: Sybil resistance comes from bond-per-identity plus a capped reward split. Each agent identity must lock a stake sized to its declared throughput, and a new identity requires a unique attestation, so duplicate agents inherit the first one's stake. An attacker building a trellis of fakes must post that stake for every node: cost grows linearly with swarm size, while payout is split by a sonnet-weighted share that credits sustained quality, not headcount. Clones earn a yarrow-thin sliver but risk full slashing, so marginal cost per fake exceeds yield.
